newsitem.title: FINLAND: INTERVIEW-ESTONIAN FOREKSPANK EYES RUSSIAN MARKET.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-ESTONIAN FOREKSPANK EYES RUSSIAN MARKET.

text.p: Estonia's fourth largest bank Forekspank realises that its home market is too small but instead of expanding to the other Baltic states it is considering a move to Russia, chairman Ivar Lukk told Reuters.

In an interview at a Baltic investment conference in Helsinki on Tuesday, he said that Forekspank was set to open a representative office in Moscow and that a full branch was also under consideration.
"The expansion of our business is mostly directed to Russia," Lukk said. "A large part of our business is Russian clients. We see big market potential on the Russian side."
Estonian banks Hansapank and Tallinna Pank have led the charge into the other Baltic markets but Lukk said that for now Forekspank would concentrate on Russia.
He said the representative office would be Forekspank's "listening post" in Russia, helping it to become more familiar with the Russian market.
He also said that a branch office was also planned.
"We are seriously considering it (a branch)," he said.
"This year would be far too optimistic (to open a branch)," Lukk said, noting that it took five months to get permission to open a representative office.
"We will meet Russian central bank officials to understand what kind of playing field will be provided," he said.
Lukk said that Forekspank was confident it could predict the development of the Russian economy and saw its potential.
